all.purpose: Prepared public News Lab API response built from the durable published shelf first. Story Objects may enrich the shelf, but they must never block cache freshness.

policy.sourceUse: Use RSS feeds, publisher pages, official records, and source links as collection/provenance inputs. The Writer drafts from the Story Dossier.
policy.copyright: Do not copy publisher article text or publisher images into the tile body.
policy.images: Use local or previously selected licensed images during worker finish mode; richer image lookup runs outside the public request path.
policy.duplicatePrevention: Several outlet reports become one original Censored Expressions story instead of several duplicate tiles.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.summary: Trump hits Canada with 50% tariffs in major trade escalation To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, has.
body: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations.

But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield. Trade between the EU and Canada is on the rise and may now accelerate Image: Sean Kilpatrick/empics/picture alliance The latest salvo in US President Donald Trump's freewheeling trade war could have disastrous effects for Canadian business.

Trump's planned 50% tariff on a range of imported goods ranges from wine to hockey sticks but does not include other key sectors such as energy, potash and fish. It is expected to impact about 5%, or $20 billion (€17.5 billion) worth, of goods and "the impact could be devastating for the people in businesses involved," Julian Karaguesian, an economics lecturer from Canada's McGill University, told DW.

ownedStories.title: James Alters the Playoff Race
ownedStories.summary: After deciding " I still truly love this game, and I have more to give," James chose the 76ers, committing to a fourth NBA team as he searches for a fifth NBA championship before retirement.
body: LeBron James, after considering retirement, is continuing his NBA career with the 76ers.

James is taking a two-year, $8 million deal, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN LeBron chooses 76ers, calls it his 'last decision'. James made nearly $53 million with the Los Angeles Lakers last season.

In a series of posts on X, James addressed his decision-making, writing that he initially thought he was done playing after the 2025-26 season before taking time to decide on his future. "I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game," he wrote.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: James Alters the Playoff Race
ownedStories.summary: After deciding " I still truly love this game, and I have more to give," James chose the 76ers, committing to a fourth NBA team as he searches for a fifth NBA championship before retirement.
body: LeBron James, after considering retirement, is continuing his NBA career with the 76ers.

James is taking a two-year, $8 million deal, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN LeBron chooses 76ers, calls it his 'last decision'. James made nearly $53 million with the Los Angeles Lakers last season.

In a series of posts on X, James addressed his decision-making, writing that he initially thought he was done playing after the 2025-26 season before taking time to decide on his future. "I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game," he wrote.

ownedStories.title: Trump Alters the Playoff Race
ownedStories.summary: Trump hits Canada with 50% tariffs in major trade escalation To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, has.
body: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations.

But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield. Trade between the EU and Canada is on the rise and may now accelerate Image: Sean Kilpatrick/empics/picture alliance The latest salvo in US President Donald Trump's freewheeling trade war could have disastrous effects for Canadian business.

Trump's planned 50% tariff on a range of imported goods ranges from wine to hockey sticks but does not include other key sectors such as energy, potash and fish. It is expected to impact about 5%, or $20 billion (€17.5 billion) worth, of goods and "the impact could be devastating for the people in businesses involved," Julian Karaguesian, an economics lecturer from Canada's McGill University, told DW.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Trump Alters the Playoff Race
ownedStories.summary: Trump hits Canada with 50% tariffs in major trade escalation To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, has.
body: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations.

But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield. Trade between the EU and Canada is on the rise and may now accelerate Image: Sean Kilpatrick/empics/picture alliance The latest salvo in US President Donald Trump's freewheeling trade war could have disastrous effects for Canadian business.

Trump's planned 50% tariff on a range of imported goods ranges from wine to hockey sticks but does not include other key sectors such as energy, potash and fish. It is expected to impact about 5%, or $20 billion (€17.5 billion) worth, of goods and "the impact could be devastating for the people in businesses involved," Julian Karaguesian, an economics lecturer from Canada's McGill University, told DW.

ownedStories.summary: Plus, email as turn-based combat (which is really just regular email). Team Spino/Boltray Games Welcome to our latest roundup of what's going on in the indie game space.
body: Those videos include the only-known footage of the Sega Saturn's reveal and Sony announcing the price of the original PlayStation (both from the 1995 edition ). This isn't necessarily directly related to indie games, though some are mentioned in the E3 materials.

Developer: Team Spino Publishers: Team Spino, Boltray Games Platform: Steam (Windows; playable on Steam Deck) Price: Usually $20, with a 10 percent discount until July 30 A pair of comments on a Reddit thread for this trailer sums up just why video games are the best. "This looks stupid as all f***," one user said.

ownedStories.title: James Alters the Playoff Race
ownedStories.summary: After deciding " I still truly love this game, and I have more to give," James chose the 76ers, committing to a fourth NBA team as he searches for a fifth NBA championship before retirement.
body: LeBron James, after considering retirement, is continuing his NBA career with the 76ers.

James is taking a two-year, $8 million deal, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN LeBron chooses 76ers, calls it his 'last decision'. James made nearly $53 million with the Los Angeles Lakers last season.

In a series of posts on X, James addressed his decision-making, writing that he initially thought he was done playing after the 2025-26 season before taking time to decide on his future. "I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game," he wrote.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Google Loses Final Appeal Over EU Android Fine
ownedStories.summary: Paramount Faces Drawn-Out Battle With State AGs: ‘They Saw the Writing on the Wall’ is being tracked through 1 report, with emphasis on government action, officials involved, and public consequences.
body: Paramount conceded that its fight with 12 state AGs will not end in a quick knockout, but will drag on for months.
The public issue now turns on the officials involved, the next formal action, and whether the decision produces a measurable policy result.
The next local update should add the official timeline, public safety effect, road or service impact, and any instructions residents need.
Only a few days ago, the states’ antitrust challenge to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger still looked like a speed bump. Now, it looks more like siege warfare — as Param.
The record centers on the EU antitrust case against Google's Android business, the size of the fine, the appeal process, and what the ruling means for technology regulation in Europe.

boardVisibility.rule: News Lab board accumulates approved CE Media articles instead of replacing them early. Articles remain visible for 7 days, unless a newer same-story replacement passes review or the board reaches its limit. Expired articles leave news tabs but remain searchable.

boardDatePolicy.rule: New approved articles add to the board instead of replacing older approved articles. Same-story updates replace the prior tile. Articles leave news tabs only after the 7-day board window expires or the board reaches its limit; expired articles remain searchable.
